matchups.name: instant reanimator
matchups.stance_rationale: Their whole deck is a graveyard: Goryo's Vengeance and Ephemerate rebuy Atraxa, Grand Unifier off a Faithful Mending discard. Graveyard exile answers the engine rather than the body, and Consign to Memory answers the Atraxa trigger that draws them back into the game.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: answers our colorless spells and, more importantly, our triggered abilities; three copies at one mana.
{U} against a blue spell - every counter and every threat in our 60 except the black removal.
a sweeper that costs them nothing, because their threat lives in the graveyard and ours live on the battlefield.
they board graveyard hate against us too, for Psychic Frog's exile-three ability and Murktide-class delve.

opponent_plan.posture_why: A turn-two or turn-three Atraxa off Goryo's Vengeance ends the game on card advantage alone; the disruption they carry exists to buy the one turn the reanimation needs, not to grind.

key_cards.why: reanimated on turn two she draws four cards and blocks everything; the enters trigger is the game, not the body.
one mana answers the colorless half of our board and any trigger we build a turn around.

their deck is four colors of blue and white; Dispute costs one against everything that matters and nothing in their board answers an instant.

play_plan.goldfish_for: Nihil Spellbomb, then hold it until they discard Atraxa.
play_plan.watch_for: An untapped Marsh Flats on turn two is Goryo's Vengeance mana, not Solitude.
play_plan.posture_why: Their threat is faster than ours, so the graveyard has to go before we start attacking.

matchups.name: broodscale bloodchief
matchups.stance_rationale: Basking Broodscale plus Blade of the Bloodchief is an ability-based infinite, so the answers that work are the ones that turn abilities off or sweep the enablers rather than the ones that target a creature. Dress Down and Toxic Deluge both do that, and both cost us our own board.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: one more mana for each spell after the first, against a deck whose plan is a threat plus held-up interaction.
{G} instant, destroys an artifact - our Engineered Explosives and our Nihil Spellbomb are both artifacts.
a fourth copy alongside the two maindeck, so the free-spell half of our 60 is taxed in every game.
boarded against the graveyard decks, it also stops nothing of ours; it is here because it comes in on the play by habit.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Vexing Bauble in the maindeck and Damping Sphere from the board tax the free spells and the fetch-heavy manabase, so the combo assembles behind a soft prison rather than racing it.

key_cards.why: the combo half that has to resolve; every other card in the deck is a way to find it or protect it.
counters any spell cast for no mana - that is three Force of Negation and three evoked Subtlety in our 60.
taxes our second spell each turn, which is exactly how a tempo deck holds up interaction and deploys at once.
answers our Engineered Explosives and our Nihil Spellbomb for one mana at instant speed.

survives_opposing_board.why: Kozilek's Command and Ancient Stirrings are the deck's engine and Consign answers the colorless one; nothing in their board counters a one-mana blue instant.
Nature's Claim answers it, but a Claim spent on Explosives is a Claim not spent on the Spellbomb, and Explosives is sacrificed at instant speed in response.
Basking Broodscale with no abilities is a vanilla creature, and the enchantment is gone at end of turn before their Nature's Claim matters.

play_plan.goldfish_for: Engineered Explosives at one for Blade of the Bloodchief.
play_plan.watch_for: Urza's Saga chapter three fetches Haywire Mite or Walking Ballista, not a combo piece.
play_plan.posture_why: They win from an empty board, so our clock is worthless until the combo is answered.

matchups.self_cost: Dress Down turns off Psychic Frog's pump and its exile-three flying, Quantum Riddler's flying, and Orcish Bowmasters' amass trigger; Toxic Deluge for two kills Orcish Bowmasters and Quantum Riddler and everything else we have except a Frog that has already grown and Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student, whose 0/3 body survives -2/-2 as a 0/1.

matchups.name: eldrazi ramp

opposing_sideboard_in.why: {3} for every spell, against a deck whose interaction costs one and two - it is the hardest card in the field for us.
set to one it counters four Fatal Push, four Thoughtseize, two Spell Snare, two Consign to Memory and two Tamiyo.

free, and this is the matchup where our only boarded artifact would otherwise be safe.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Every card is either a mana source or something that ends the game on resolution, so the plan is to be casting a seven-drop before a tempo deck has assembled a clock.

survives_opposing_board.why: a 2/2 body against a deck whose cheapest interaction from the board is a three-mana Trinisphere; Endurance can block it but cannot remove it, and the static ability has already done its work.
Kozilek's Command, Sowing Mycospawn and Emrakul's cast trigger are all colorless or triggered, so one mana answers the most expensive card in their deck.

play_plan.keep: Two lands with a blue source and either Harbinger of the Seas or two counters.

Fetchlands become Islands and can no longer fetch; the manabase collapses to two Island, one Swamp and a field of Islands, so Fatal Push, Thoughtseize, Drown in the Loch, Sheoldred's Edict and Orcish Bowmasters all become uncastable off anything but the single Swamp. That is why four Fatal Push leave for it rather than something cheaper.

every counter we hold is blue and one mana is what it costs them to answer it.
boarded against us, it also blanks Psychic Frog's exile-three flying and any delve plan.
free evoke that destroys our Nihil Spellbomb or Engineered Explosives before the cascade turn.

the cascade trigger is a triggered ability, so this is the one answer in the field their Mystical Dispute cannot profitably race - both cost one.

Nihil Spellbomb answers it, Consign to Memory answers the Archon trigger, and Toxic Deluge answers the body once it is already there - at the cost of ours.

nonbasic lands are Islands, which strands the black half of our deck behind one Swamp.
counters any spell cast for no mana, aimed at Force of Negation and evoked Subtlety.

three copies, and the mirror of our own plan: it answers Archon triggers and our Quantum Riddler alike.

counters our Force of Negation and our evoked Subtlety, the two free answers we hold up.

their own copies are blue and cannot counter ours; Archon of Cruelty's enters trigger is the most expensive triggered ability in the field and this answers it for one mana.
a sorcery with no target, so Consign to Memory and Vexing Bauble both miss it, and paying life gets past Archon of Cruelty's toughness where damage would not.

play_plan.keep: Two lands, a Thoughtseize or a counter, and a graveyard answer if the hand has one.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Nihil Spellbomb, held for the Persist rather than cracked on sight.
play_plan.watch_for: A turn-one Faithless Looting means Archon of Cruelty on turn two, so counters go up now.
play_plan.posture_why: Their threat arrives before ours and outclasses it, so the graveyard has to go first.

matchups.self_cost: Toxic Deluge for four or more is what it takes to kill Archon of Cruelty, and that number kills every creature we control several times over; boarding it means accepting that our own board is a cost we pay to reset theirs.

matchups.name: allosaurus combo
matchups.stance_rationale: Their protection is Veil of Summer and Pact of Negation, which answer counterspells but not triggered abilities, so a Summoner's Pact upkeep trigger is still a legal Consign to Memory target through Veil - but countering it does not punish them. Summoner's Pact's oracle text is one triggered ability: 'At the beginning of your next upkeep, pay {2}{G}{G}. If you don't, you lose the game.' Per CR 701.6a, a countered ability's effects do not occur at all, including its own loss-the-game clause, so countering that trigger cancels the payment demand and the loss together and hands them a free pass. Consign to Memory must never be pointed at the Pact trigger. Its real use in this matchup is countering Atraxa, Grand Unifier's enters trigger if the Neoform or Eldritch Evolution line resolves into her, which denies the card-advantage payoff without stopping the body; Thoughtseize on turn one, taking the Pact or the Neoform before it is cast, is the actual answer to the combo.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: one mana against a blue spell; every counter we hold and every threat we play is blue.
two more copies on top of the two maindeck, so four of their cards blank our counterspells outright.
one-mana instant artifact removal; it is aimed at graveyard hate but hits anything we board.
a fair plan for post-board games where the combo has been answered twice.

opponent_plan.posture_why: The deck wins on turn one or two through a hand of free spells, and its interaction is entirely defensive: Veil of Summer and Pact of Negation exist to make that turn stick, not to answer us.

key_cards.why: cast for free by pitching two green cards, it is the body every combo line converts.
spells they control cannot be countered this turn, which turns off nine counterspells in our 60.
four copies at one mana against every blue card we have, on the turn they are comboing.
a boarded threat for the games where we have answered the combo and they need a fair plan.

survives_opposing_board.why: Veil of Summer stops spells being countered, not triggered abilities, so this card still resolves through it. That does not make the Pact trigger a good target: per CR 701.6a a countered ability's effects, including its own 'if you don't pay, you lose the game' clause, do not occur, so countering it removes their loss condition instead of enforcing it. What survives Veil here is the option to counter Atraxa, Grand Unifier's enters trigger if their combo line resolves into her, denying the draw without stopping the body.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and two pieces of one-mana disruption; anything slower loses to a turn-two kill.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Thoughtseize on turn one, taking the Neoform over the Rider.
play_plan.watch_for: A green source untapped on our turn is Veil of Summer, so counters are dead that turn.
play_plan.posture_why: They kill through an empty board on turn two, so our clock never matters.

matchups.name: creatures toolbox
matchups.stance_rationale: Toxic Deluge and Dress Down are the two cards that answer an assembled engine, and both are symmetric: Deluge for two is set where it kills the great bulk of their creature suite - the toolbox curve is dominated by one- and two-toughness bodies (THEORY, read off the pulled 75s; not a counted statistic) - and that number kills almost everything we have too - Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student's 0/3 body is the exception, surviving -2/-2 as a 0/1. Consign to Memory is the one-sided card in the plan and it only reaches the Craterhoof Behemoth trigger.
matchups.self_cost: Toxic Deluge at two kills Psychic Frog and Orcish Bowmasters along with their board, so it is cast from behind rather than on curve; Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student's 0/3 body survives as a 0/1. Dress Down turns off Psychic Frog's pump and its exile-three flying and Orcish Bowmasters' amass trigger for the turn it is out. Both are the price of answering a combo that does not care about our clock.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: ten of ten boards at two or three copies. Psychic Frog, Orcish Bowmasters and Kaito are all mana value 2 or less, so their generic removal is fully live against our threats without them boarding anything matchup-specific.

ten of ten boards at one copy. 'Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated' turns off both Engineered Explosives and both Nihil Spellbomb, which is four of our fifteen board slots, and it is why neither is boarded in this row.

eight of ten boards at exactly two copies. It counters a spell cast for no mana, which is our three pitched Force of Negation and our three evoked Subtlety - six of the sixty. It taxes rather than blanks: both are still castable for mana, and Consign to Memory for {U} counters the Bauble trigger itself.

seven of ten boards at one to three copies. A flash 3/4 reach blocker that outclasses every creature we have, and its enters trigger puts our graveyard on the bottom of the library, which shrinks Drown in the Loch and denies Psychic Frog the three cards it exiles for flying.

six of ten boards at one copy. It fights a creature we don't control with flying, which is an unconditional two-mana kill on Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student, a 0/3 with printed flying. It does not answer Psychic Frog: the Frog is a 1/2 with no printed flying and we simply decline to exile three cards on their turn, leaving the trigger no legal target.

six of ten boards at one copy. 'You have hexproof' blanks all four Thoughtseize, and the prevention clause walls Orcish Bowmasters against their other creatures. It is a {1}{W} 0/4 artifact creature, so Fatal Push kills it and Spell Snare counters it.

nine of ten boards at one copy, and close to a blank against us - nothing in our sixty is cast from anywhere but hand. Recorded because it is the card most likely to be misread as relevant; it is a 1/3 that dies to Fatal Push.

five of ten boards at one copy, and it does much less than it looks like. Mode two removes counters from the PLAYER, so it never reaches Kaito's loyalty.

seven of ten boards at one copy. A three-mana planeswalker that grinds one-for-one against a board of small creatures and is a creature everywhere but the battlefield, so it is a legal Fatal Push and Spell Snare target on the stack.

one of ten boards, and recorded because of what it does rather than how common it is. Against a mono-UB deck it makes their spell uncounterable and gives them and their permanents hexproof from blue and black for the turn, which turns off every interactive card in our seventy-five at once and cantrips while doing it.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Devoted Druid plus Vizier of Remedies is unbounded mana the turn it assembles and Nature's Rhythm puts Craterhoof Behemoth onto the battlefield to end the game on the same turn, so they outrun us rather than grind.

key_cards.why: combo half one, four copies in ten of ten lists: '{T}: Add {G}' plus 'put a -1/-1 counter on this creature: untap this creature'.

combo half two: the -1/-1 counter is reduced to none, so the untap is free and the mana is unbounded. It costs {1}{W} and they run one white land, but it never needs casting - Nature's Rhythm and Fiend Artisan put it onto the battlefield.

four copies in ten of ten lists. It searches for ANY creature card and puts it onto the battlefield, so it is both the colorless tutor for the white half and the Craterhoof Behemoth delivery, and it has harmonize from the graveyard.
eight of ten lists at one copy. The enters trigger, not the body, is the kill: trample and +X/+X for the number of creatures they control.

survives_opposing_board.why: a sorcery, so Collector Ouphe does not reach it and there is no permanent for Force of Vigor or the sacrifice creatures to destroy. It is the only sweeper in our box that is immune to their whole artifact-hate package.
one mana at instant speed, and their board carries no counterspell except Vexing Bauble, which does not see a spell cast for mana.

an enchantment, and only three of ten boards carry Force of Vigor while the sacrifice creatures - Guerrilla Gorilla in five lists, Outland Liberator in the other five - are sorcery-speed or cost mana. It is sacrificed at the end step anyway, so it is rarely worth answering.
Collector Ouphe is a one-of in ten of ten boards and stops activated abilities of artifacts, which is the only way Explosives does anything. Not boarded here for that reason.
same Collector Ouphe clause, and their graveyard use is thin anyway - Fiend Artisan's static count and Nature's Rhythm's harmonize. Not boarded here.

not by a card of theirs but by their mana. Basic Forests, Birds of Paradise and Devoted Druid are untouched, and Leyline of Abundance and Badgermole Cub turn a neutered Dryad Arbor or Delighted Halfling back into green. Not boarded here.
zero blue cards appear in any of the ten lists, main or board, so it never gets its {2} discount and is a three-mana soft counter in a tempo deck. Not boarded here.

matchups.self_cost: Toxic Deluge takes our own two-drops, and Engineered Explosives at one kills Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student. Cutting three Force of Negation for them also removes the only free interaction we have on their turn, which is the turn Voice of Victory would have stopped us anyway.
notes: Everything recorded here from game 9c9d2f2bf6714b689ca60fd62c1acbfc is two turns of one game, released before a single attack. It is evidence about the opening and about how the deck was identified, and it says nothing about how the matchup plays out.

Guide of Souls plus Galvanic Discharge is the tell that separates this row from boros aggro. Both decks run Guide of Souls; the Discharge is the energy card, and it is not in the boros aggro row's key cards. In game 9c9d2f2b a turn-one Thoughtseize on the play saw Voice of Victory, Solitude, Guide of Souls, Galvanic Discharge, Marsh Flats and two Flooded Strand - the hand named the archetype before the board had shown anything.

Take Voice of Victory over Guide of Souls with a turn-one Thoughtseize. "Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn" blanks all eleven reactive cards this 60 is built on - 2 Counterspell, 3 Force of Negation, 2 Spell Snare, 3 Subtlety, 1 Drown in the Loch - for as long as it lives, and Mobilize 2 makes it a three-body attack on top. Guide of Souls, Galvanic Discharge and Solitude each cost us a card to answer, but none of them turns the deck off. This is the opening-hand form of the decision `self_cost` already records for the three Force of Negation. It is a judgement call and not a demonstrated result: game 9c9d2f2b took the Voice and was released on turn two, so the line was never played out.

They spend life on their own manabase. In game 9c9d2f2b they cracked Marsh Flats for an untapped Sacred Foundry at 2 life on turn one to cast Guide of Souls, and were at 17 on their own first turn. Guide of Souls buys those points back, so price a race against a life total they are willing to pay down, not against twenty.

matchups.name: pinnacle affinity

matchups.name: devoted combo
matchups.stance_rationale: Fatal Push and Spell Snare do the one-for-one work maindeck, but neither answers an engine already assembled, and the two cards in the box that do are both symmetric. Toxic Deluge for two kills Birds of Paradise, Delighted Halfling, Devoted Druid, Badgermole Cub, Vizier of Remedies, Duskwatch Recruiter, Collector Ouphe, Sylvan Safekeeper, an eighteen-copies-in-ten-lists Dryad Arbor and the 1/1 land Badgermole Cub earthbends - it is the only sweeper in the box that is also land destruction here - and it does it as a sorcery with no permanent for Boseiju, Force of Vigor, Abrupt Decay or Guerrilla Gorilla to destroy, and with no targeting for Crystal Barricade or Sylvan Safekeeper's shroud to dodge. Dress Down for two turns Devoted Druid back into a vanilla 0/2 at flash speed. Consign to Memory is the one-sided card in the plan and it only reaches the triggers, chiefly Craterhoof Behemoth's.
matchups.self_cost: Toxic Deluge at two kills Psychic Frog and Orcish Bowmasters along with their board and costs two life, so it is cast from behind rather than on curve; Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student is a 0/3 and survives -2/-2 as a 0/1. Dress Down strips Psychic Frog's pump and its exile-three flying, Tamiyo's flying and Orcish Bowmasters' trigger for as long as it is out. Both are the price of answering a combo that never has to interact with our clock.

one mana answers the colorless half of our board and any trigger we build a turn around; four copies in most boards.
sweeps Psychic Frog, Orcish Bowmasters and Tamiyo at once while their own threat is safely in the graveyard.

an instant their own Consign cannot touch (it counters triggered abilities or colorless spells, not blue instants); it answers the Atraxa enters trigger for one mana.

nothing in their seventy-five hard-counters an instant outright; it costs one against Atraxa, Psychic Frog, Faithful Mending and Ephemerate, though their own Mystical Dispute is the same trade at parity.

ten of ten boards, at two or three copies. A cheap body that also answers a resolved threat of ours.
ten of ten boards, at one to four copies. One mana against our colorless artifacts and any triggered ability.
ten of ten boards, at two copies. Sweeps our whole two-drop board once they have already committed their own wide start.

a boarded body that also answers a resolved threat of ours once it lands.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and two pieces of cheap interaction; a hand with no turn-two answer is behind before Territorial Kavu resolves.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Toxic Deluge for two, cast once their Domain threats have already grown.
play_plan.watch_for: An open blue source is Stubborn Denial; sequence removal before counters where possible.
play_plan.posture_why: Their curve is faster than ours, so surviving to a Toxic Deluge turn beats trading removal one for one.

sideboard_audit.why: One mana for a triggered ability or a colorless spell, which is the widest answer in the box against this field: Atraxa and Archon of Cruelty enters triggers (instant reanimator, reanimator, esper goryo), the Living End cascade trigger, Primeval Titan's fetch, Urza's Saga chapters, Kozilek's Command, and the Craterhoof Behemoth enters trigger that is how devoted combo and creatures toolbox actually kill. Against allosaurus combo it reaches through Veil of Summer the same way, because a triggered ability is not a spell, but only for Atraxa's enters trigger if their Neoform or Eldritch Evolution line resolves into her - countering the Summoner's Pact upkeep trigger itself does not punish them. Per CR 701.6a a countered ability's effects, including its own 'if you don't pay, you lose the game' clause, do not occur, so that specific target must never be taken. Two copies here rather than four because two are already maindeck.

Flash, draws a card, and every creature loses all abilities while it is out. It is the answer to the three ability-based engines in the field that removal does not reach: Basking Broodscale with Blade of the Bloodchief stops being a combo, Primeval Titan stops fetching, and a Devoted Druid becomes a vanilla 0/2 in both halves of the split devoted combo / creatures toolbox archetype. One copy, because each of those matchups also has counterspell, sweeper or Harbinger of the Seas answers in this board, so Dress Down is the third line of defence rather than the first.

The only sweeper in the box that scales to a mana value rather than to toughness, which is what the cheap-permanent decks in this field need. At one it takes Ocelot Pride, Ragavan, Mox Opal, Welding Jar and Blade of the Bloodchief; at two it takes Ruby Medallion, Artist's Talent and the whole two-drop half of a fair board. Our two colors cap sunburst at two, which is why it is not boarded against anything that needs three.

Nonbasic lands are Islands. Against eldrazi ramp, amulet titan and pinnacle affinity that is not a tax but a shutdown - Eldrazi Temple, Simic Growth Chamber and Urza's Saga all stop being what they are. Three copies because it has to arrive by turn three to matter and because Dismember and Galvanic Discharge answer the first one. It is the most symmetric card in the box: it turns our own seventeen nonbasics into Islands, which is why every row that boards it also boards out the black removal.

One mana against a blue spell, three against anything else. The blue-heavy half of this field is over 20pp and the mirror is decided by which side's counter costs less, which is exactly the question this card answers - including the esper goryo shell, whose fair half is the same Psychic Frog / Quantum Riddler package we run. Three copies because in the mirror and against instant reanimator it is the best card in the box, not a role-player.

Instant-speed exile of a whole graveyard for one mana up front and zero to use, which is what the graveyard decks in this field need: it is held for the Goryo's Vengeance, the Persist, the cascade trigger or the Past in Flames, not cracked on sight. Two copies rather than three because Consign to Memory and Mystical Dispute overlap on the same matchups and a third Spellbomb is the worst of the three cards in the games where they do not draw the engine.

Pay X life, all creatures get -X/-X: no targeting, no damage, and no mana value cap, so it answers the go-wide boards and the oversized ones alike, including 45c aggro's Domain-scaled Territorial Kavu and Scion of Draco. It is the only card in the box that beats a Leyline of the Guildpact board, a resolved Archon of Cruelty and a Vengevine loop with the same card, and against both halves of the devoted combo / creatures toolbox split it is also land destruction, because Dryad Arbor and a Badgermole-earthbent land are creatures. Two copies, and it is symmetric every time - the rows that board it record what it costs us.

deck_tech.name: Psychic Frog into Quantum Riddler
deck_tech.quirk: Emptying our own hand is the Frog's cost and the switch that turns Quantum Riddler on.
loop: discard to Psychic Frog until one or fewer cards are left in hand
Quantum Riddler's replacement now adds one to every draw we make
the Frog connects and its trigger draws two instead of one
discard the surplus back to the Frog for another counter
the hand is empty again before the next attack

lines.why: Two cards a hit beats a deck that answers one threat a turn. Exiling three from the yard for flying comes before the counters do: an unblocked Frog is the whole engine.
Every card discarded here was a removal spell we needed. Against a turn-four clock the Frog is a blocker and the counters are a luxury.

deck_tech.name: Which counter answers what
deck_tech.quirk: Three of the four are conditional, and the wrong one in hand against the wrong deck is a blank card.

lines.mode: Consign to Memory, for the trigger
lines.why: It counters a triggered ability or a colourless spell. Hold it for the cascade trigger, the Primeval Titan trigger or an Eldrazi cast trigger, never for the spell that made it.

lines.mode: Spell Snare, at mana value two exactly
lines.why: Two and only two. Goryo's Vengeance is two and so is their own Psychic Frog; a one-mana cantrip and a three-mana threat are both out of range.

lines.mode: Force of Negation, free on their turn
lines.why: The free mode is noncreature only and only on their turn, so it answers the combo turn and nothing on ours. A blue card from hand is the cost.
The only one with no condition attached, so it is what answers the threat the other three cannot. Spend the narrow counters first, while their targets are still on the table.

deck_tech.name: The Frog clock, or the Harbinger lock
deck_tech.quirk: Which half of the deck this hand is: a two-mana threat that draws cards, or land denial that ends the game on its own.

lines.why: Nonbasic lands are Islands, which turns off Tron, Eldrazi Temple and every bounce land at once. It is the plan against a deck whose mana is its deck.
A turn-two threat that replaces itself beats a deck holding one answer a turn. Tamiyo is the second one-drop and flips once the Frog starts drawing.

meta_calls.why: Removal is dead against a deck whose only creature is the payoff. The free counter and Spell Snare answer Goryo's Vengeance, Neoform and Basking Broodscale at two mana.
meta_calls.cost: Ragavan and Guide of Souls both resolve, and every fair matchup gets worse on the draw. Devoted combo is deliberately out of the cluster: its engine is all mana value 2 creatures, so cutting Fatal Push is wrong there.

meta_calls.why: A third Spellbomb is the answer that can be cracked in response to the cascade trigger, before the Living End returns anything, and it costs one colourless to deploy.
meta_calls.cost: Dress Down was the one clean answer to Basking Broodscale and to Devoted Druid.

meta_calls.why: Their Harbinger turns every dual into an Island and the black half of the sixty stops casting. Basics are the only lands it does not touch.
meta_calls.cost: One fewer untapped black source on turn one and one fewer surveil land, which is the mana this deck's fetch counts were built around.

gaps.why: Veil of Summer is four cards across their maindeck and board (two and two in the BesmirchTheKing 75, tournament 6a17baa7-6295-4907-b49e-83323a23d046) and it blanks three Counterspell, two Spell Snare, three Force of Negation and two Drown in the Loch for the turn they combo, on top of three Pact of Negation. That is ten of our counterspell-and-removal answers turned off by one one-mana card. This gap is worse than an earlier pass of this plan claimed: countering the Summoner's Pact upkeep trigger with Consign to Memory does not punish them. Summoner's Pact's oracle text is a single triggered ability ('At the beginning of your next upkeep, pay {2}{G}{G}. If you don't, you lose the game.'), and per CR 701.6a a countered ability's effects do not occur at all, so countering it cancels the payment demand and the loss together - it is a line that helps the Pact controller, not one that kills them, and it must not be played. The one real line through Veil is Subtlety on whichever creature spell it evokes into. Consign to Memory's only genuine use here is countering Atraxa, Grand Unifier's enters trigger if the Neoform or Eldritch Evolution line resolves into her, which denies the card-advantage payoff but does not stop the body from resolving. Neither is a card we can count on drawing by turn two, so pre-emptive Thoughtseize on the Pact or the Neoform before it is cast remains the more reliable answer, and this matchup has no reliable way to punish a resolved combo turn once Veil is up.
